messages.text: I’ll read the assignment and its ExecPlan first, then work only within that lane’s stated scope and return the required handback report.

The assigned worktree is present at the policy base and has no lane commits or saved decisions yet. I’ve read the required rules; I’m bringing in the two audit-policy commits now, then I’ll review each usage test from its provenance and body.

The first reviewed file is a direct unit suite for `LocalInferenceEngine`, added with a general refactor rather than a defect fix. I’m retaining its one genuinely tricky scope rule: an unresolved inner shadow must hide a known outer binding and the outer binding must return after scope exit; the remaining eight tests restate direct alias, cap, or snapshot behavior.

The usage regressions reviewed so far are tied to concrete fixes, including stale cross-request syntax/import data and duplicated C++ candidate scans; I’ve tagged those tests and committed the first pruning pass. I’m now checking the small resolver and receiver suites for direct helper checks that can be removed and for any other fix-backed cases that need tags.

The receiver allocation cases form one useful cross-language feature family, so I’m replacing that inline matrix with a golden that queries `query_code` over real C++, Go, Kotlin, PHP, Python, Ruby, Rust, and Scala files. The separate receiver-budget boundary and the language-specific shadowing/uncertainty cases remain under review as tricky behavior.

The filtered golden build is compiling the root package and language crates on this worktree’s normal Cargo target; it hasn’t reported an error. Once it finishes, I’ll inspect the rendered output before accepting it and rerun the case without bless.
The compile is still active and quiet after the initial dependency build. It is compiling the large analyzer/test target, so I’m letting this single filtered run finish before moving on.

The two golden areas are now drafted: direct receiver allocation results and cross-module/cross-language usage relevance. The allocation fixture is being compiled with the first filtered run; I’ve also copied the existing same-module fixture into the new golden tree so all four ranking cases use real project files.

Both golden cases have been generated and their snapshots reviewed. The usage relevance golden preserves all four ranking scenarios; the receiver golden reduces a large JSON payload to the exact result type, owner, source/allocation lines, and query provenance. I’ve removed the superseded inline examples and kept the budget-boundary checks.

`cargo fmt --all` is still running without diagnostic output, likely competing with the other active lane builds. I’m waiting for it to finish before refreshing snapshots and running the lane’s required clippy check.
